decisions.rationale: Intended Mega: Scizor. Lead Politoed+Archaludon: Drizzle overrides Zard-Y Drought so Archaludon fires one-turn Electro Shot (SE 2x, possible OHKO) at Zard-Y or Talonflame. Back Garganacl provides Wide Guard to block Heat Wave/Rock Slide spread and Rock Slide 4x on Fire/Flying; Purifying Salt immune to Sleep Powder when switched in. Mega Scizor cleans late with Technician Bullet Punch. If Raichu appears, pivot to Draco Meteor or Hydro Pump on Zard-Y instead.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 plan: Rain core Politoed+Archaludon lead, Garganacl+Mega Scizor back. Politoed Drizzle (90 Spe, slower than Zard-Y 132-167) overrides Drought since slower weather wins. Electro Shot in rain = one-turn, SE 2x on Fire/Flying, possible OHKO range 38-122% on Zard-Y, 52-183% on Talonflame. Garganacl Rock Slide 4x on Zard-Y (54-188% even through spread), Purifying Salt immune to Sleep Powder. Scizor-Mega: Technician Bullet Punch for late cleanup, Close Combat 2x on Goodra-Hisui. Key threats to watch: Raichu Lightning Rod redirects Electro Shot (use Draco Meteor/Hydro Pump instead), Venusaur raw Spe 100-132 can outspeed Archaludon 123 and Sleep Powder first (Protect scout or bring Garganacl in for immunity), Talonflame Gale Wings Brave Bird priority. Opponent team has no entry hazards. Opponent speed tiers: Talonflame 160-195 > Raichu 143-178 > Garchomp 134-169 > Zard-Y 132-167 > Venusaur 100-132 (Chlorophyll doubles in sun but rain blocks) > Goodra-Hisui 80-112. My speed: Noivern 192 > Scizor 95 (base) > Archaludon 123 > Politoed 90 > Garganacl 55. If opponent adapts to rain lead in game 2, consider Grimmsnarl lead for Fake Out+screens or Noivern for speed control.

decisions.rationale: Intended Mega is Charizard Y. Charizard-Raichu establishes sun while Raichu denies a disruptive first turn with Fake Out/Nuzzle and Lightning Rod discourages Electro Shot. Venusaur converts sun into fast sleep and punishes Politoed; Life Orb Garchomp supplies the endgame damage into Archaludon, Noivern, and Garganacl.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 preview plan: Mega Charizard Y is the chosen Mega. Preferred four are Charizard, Raichu, Venusaur, Garchomp: Raichu protects the sun lead from Archaludon Electric pressure and disrupts screens/rain support; Venusaur is the Chlorophyll rain punish; Garchomp is the physical cleanup answer to Archaludon/Noivern/Garganacl. Opponent has Politoed rain, Grimmsnarl dual screens, Expert Belt Archaludon, Mega Scizor, Life Orb Noivern, and Garganacl Wide Guard.

decisions.rationale: Raichu Fake Out (+3 priority) guarantees a flinch on one slot before I move. Zard-Y sun-boosted Solar Beam or Heat Wave can OHKO either Pokémon if they can't Protect. Double Protect wastes Fake Out (gone next turn) and Zard-Y's attack, giving me a free turn 2 without flinch pressure. Encore risk is real but low on turn 1 — most opponents Fake Out first. Next turn I attack freely or switch Politoed to reset Drizzle over sun.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 plan: Rain core Politoed+Archaludon lead, Garganacl+Mega Scizor back. Zard-Y Drought overrides rain when it mega evolves (Politoed Drizzle already activated, won't re-trigger until re-entry). Switching Politoed out and back re-activates Drizzle to override sun — key mid-game option. Raichu Lightning Rod redirects Electro Shot (use Draco Meteor/Hydro Pump instead). Key sun damage ranges: Draco Meteor on Zard-Y 34.6-117.6%, Solar Beam on Politoed 32.5-106.7%, Heat Wave on Archaludon 27.9-100.6% (all possible OHKO, none guaranteed). Raichu has Encore — avoid consecutive Protects when Raichu is active. Garganacl Purifying Salt immune to Sleep Powder; Scizor-Mega 4x weak to Fire from Zard-Y, do not bring in on Zard-Y sun. Opponent speed tiers: Talonflame 160-195 > Raichu 143-178 > Garchomp 134-169 > Zard-Y 132-167 > Venusaur 100-132 (Chlorophyll inactive in rain) > Goodra-Hisui 80-112. My speed: Archaludon 123 > Politoed 90 > Scizor 95 (base, 75 mega) > Garganacl 55. Turn 2 plan: no Fake Out threat, attack with Archaludon Draco Meteor on Zard-Y or switch Politoed to reset rain.

decisions.rationale: Mega Evolving immediately replaces rain with sun, making Solar Beam immediate and threatening Politoed before it can attack. Fake Out denies Archaludon's only meaningful non-Electric pressure this turn; Lightning Rod already deters Electro Shot. This cleanly pressures the rain setter while preserving the sun/Venusaur endgame.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 preview plan: Mega Charizard Y is the chosen Mega. Preferred four are Charizard, Raichu, Venusaur, Garchomp. Raichu protects sun from Archaludon Electric pressure and disrupts rain/screens; Venusaur punishes rain under sun; Garchomp is physical cleanup versus Archaludon, Noivern, and Garganacl. Opponent roster: Politoed rain support, Grimmsnarl dual screens, Expert Belt Archaludon, Mega Scizor, Life Orb Noivern, Garganacl Wide Guard.

decisions.rationale: Switch Politoed to Garganacl to preserve the rain-reset tool and avoid Thunderbolt possible OHKO + Encore lock. Garganacl resists Heat Wave (15-47%) and tanks Thunderbolt (16-55%). Archaludon Draco Meteor hits Zard-Y for 28.6-90.8%. If Archaludon falls to Heat Wave, Garganacl Rock Slide is 4x SE on Zard-Y next turn. Encore on Archaludon is manageable — switch out next turn.

Zard-Y Solar Beam has 1 PP used.

decisions.rationale: Solar Beam moves before Politoed and is a guaranteed OHKO into Politoed. Nuzzle gives durable speed control on Archaludon; Raichu’s Lightning Rod continues to deny its Electro Shot pressure. Even if Politoed risks consecutive Protect, this line preserves the favorable board while avoiding a redundant second attack into Politoed.
decisions.notebook: Opponent led Politoed + Expert Belt Archaludon and used Protect with both on turn 1. Keep Charizard/Raichu/Venusaur/Garchomp mode; use Raichu Lightning Rod to constrain Archaludon Electric attacks and target Politoed aggressively under sun. Archaludon is slower than Mega Charizard before paralysis; Nuzzle is valuable long-term speed control.

decisions.rationale: Rock Slide is guaranteed OHKO on Zard-Y at 24% (168-198% even with spread reduction). Switching Archaludon to Politoed activates Drizzle, overriding sun so Solar Beam can't fire instantly — protecting Garganacl from its only true KO threat. Archaludon at -2 SpA with Lightning Rod redirecting Electro Shot is dead weight; resetting rain is far more valuable. Garganacl risks Thunderbolt KO but Leftovers + removing Zard-Y + rain control is worth the trade.

decisions.rationale: Solar Beam is a guaranteed KO on Garganacl before it can use Rock Slide or Salt Cure. Encore acts after the slower paralyzed Archaludon: it either locks Protect or locks its chosen attack, both improving the remaining endgame. Do not risk leaving Garganacl alive.
decisions.notebook: Opponent has Politoed with Drizzle/Sitrus and Helping Hand, Expert Belt Archaludon with Stamina, and Garganacl with Leftovers. Archaludon is Modest and has been paralyzed by Nuzzle; it revealed Draco Meteor and Protect. Keep Charizard/Raichu/Venusaur/Garchomp mode; Raichu Lightning Rod constrains Electro Shot and Encore can punish Protect.

decisions.rationale: Venusaur is the safer rain pivot: Focus Sash covers Ice Beam from full and Leaf Storm immediately threatens Politoed. Garchomp risks a likely 4x-effective Ice Beam and is more valuable for the Garganacl endgame.
decisions.notebook: Opponent has Politoed with Drizzle/Sitrus and Helping Hand, Expert Belt Archaludon with Stamina, and Garganacl with Leftovers. Archaludon is Modest, paralyzed by Nuzzle, and revealed Draco Meteor and Protect. Keep Charizard/Raichu/Venusaur/Garchomp mode; Raichu Lightning Rod constrains Electro Shot and Encore can punish Protect.

decisions.rationale: Leaf Storm does 61.4%+ min to Garganacl (48% HP = guaranteed KO). Garganacl must Protect. Ice Beam (27.3-61.9%) breaks Venusaur's Focus Sash, setting up easy KO next turn. Politoed survives Thunderbolt (max 87.3%). Encore prediction by Raichu is possible but requires giving up Thunderbolt — less likely than straightforward SE targeting.
decisions.notebook: Game 1 plan: Rain core Politoed+Archaludon lead, Garganacl+Mega Scizor back. Zard-Y fainted turn 3. Raichu Lightning Rod redirects Electro Shot — never target Raichu with Electric moves. Raichu Encore dangerous when last move was Protect — avoid being on field with Protect as last move vs Raichu. Garganacl Purifying Salt = immune to Sleep Powder. Scizor-Mega 4x weak to Fire but Zard-Y is dead — safe to bring now. Scizor-Mega Speed 75 base (slower than Politoed 90) — rely on Bullet Punch priority. Venusaur Focus Sash — must hit twice to KO. Opponent back: Talonflame (Gale Wings priority Brave Bird), Garchomp (Life Orb), Goodra-Hisui (SapSipper immune to Grass). Key speed tiers in rain: Raichu 143-178 > Venusaur 100-132 > Politoed 90 > Scizor-Mega 75 > Garganacl 55. Archaludon paralyzed (Speed 61), SpA -2 from Draco Meteor — bring back late if needed. Next turn priority: KO Venusaur (1 HP after Sash break) before it uses Sleep Powder or Leaf Storm. Watch for Raichu Encore on Garganacl if last move is Protect — switch Garganacl out or use non-Protect move to avoid lock.

decisions.rationale: Venusaur is guaranteed faster than Politoed and Leaf Storm cleanly removes the weakened Garganacl. Thunderbolt is the strongest listed immediate pressure into Politoed. Splitting targets maximizes the chance to remove both opponents and avoids letting either survive freely through a single Protect.

Garganacl's last move was Protect — Raichu Encore (outspeeds at 143–178) locks it into failing Protect before it can act. Switching to Scizor-Mega avoids Encore, brings in a fresh 4× Grass wall, and Zard-Y is dead so no Fire weakness. Politoed must Protect: both foes outspeed it (Raichu TBolt likely KOs from 55%, Venusaur can Sleep Powder 75%), and Ice Beam isn't a reliable KO (28.9–61.9%, needs ≥50%). Next turn: Bullet Punch chips Venusaur, switch Politoed→Garganacl to dodge Encore on Protect.

Archaludon paralyzed (Speed 61), SpA -2 from Draco Meteor — bring back late only if needed. Then finish Venusaur with Bullet Punch + Rock Slide/Salt Cure.

decisions.rationale: Venusaur is guaranteed faster than Politoed and Leaf Storm guarantees the KO if it does not Protect. Encore exploits Garganacl's last-used Protect, denying its damaging options and making a Politoed Protect line much easier to punish next turn.
decisions.notebook: Opponent has Politoed with Drizzle/Sitrus and Helping Hand, Expert Belt Archaludon with Stamina, and Garganacl with Leftovers. Switching Politoed to Garganacl avoids Encore lock on Protect and likely Thunderbolt KO, while Garganacl's Purifying Salt immunizes it to Sleep Powder. Next turn finish Venusaur with Bullet Punch + Rock Slide/Salt Cure. Sleep Powder 75% on Scizor is the main risk but acceptable.

decisions.rationale: Thunderbolt is guaranteed to KO Politoed from its shown HP and Raichu always moves first at equal priority. Venusaur Protect preserves it from Politoed Ice Beam and avoids exposing it while retaining Garchomp for the endgame. If Politoed risks its reduced Protect, Raichu still remains positioned to remove it next turn.

decisions.rationale: Leaf Storm guaranteed KOs Garganacl at 33%. Switching Garganacl to Politoed dodges the likely double-target (both moves fail on empty slot), Politoed's Drizzle extends rain past this turn — critical to halve Talonflame/Goodra Fire moves vs Scizor. Bullet Punch (priority +1, confirmed first) chips Venusaur to 13-30%, setting up KO next turn via Bullet Punch + Ice Beam/Helping Hand. Encore on Scizor only locks it into Bullet Punch which we're already using. Garganacl preserved at 33% for late Wide
decisions.notebook: Game 1 plan: Rain core Politoed+Archaludon lead, Garganacl+Mega Scizor back. Zard-Y fainted turn 3. Raichu Lightning Rod redirects Electro Shot — never target Raichu with Electric moves. Raichu Encore failed twice targeting switching-in slots (no last move); Encore CAN work on Pokémon with established last move. Garganacl Purifying Salt = immune to Sleep Powder. Scizor-Mega 4x resists Grass; Zard-Y dead so no Fire threat while rain active. Venusaur Focus Sash broken (at 50%). Bullet Punch does 20-37% to Venusaur. Close Combat does 56-117% to Raichu (potential KO at 58%). Leaf Storm guaranteed KOs Garganacl at 33% (61-137%). Raichu Thunderbolt ~26% to Garganacl. Opponent back: Talonflame (Gale Wings priority Brave Bird 1x on Scizor, Flare Blitz 4x on Scizor but rain halves to 2x), Garchomp (Life Orb, Ice 4x weak, Stomping Tantrum 2x SE on Scizor), Goodra-Hisui (SapSipper Grass immune, Steel/Dragon resists Ice/Fire 0.5x, Fire Blast 4x on Scizor without rain). Rain extension via Politoed Drizzle is critical — without rain Scizor faces 4x Fire moves. Archaludon paralyzed Speed 61, SpA -2 — defensive pivot only, resists Thunderbolt 0.5x and Leaf Storm 0.25x. Key speed tiers: Raichu 143-178 > Venusaur 100-132 > Politoed 90 > Scizor 105 (non-priority) > Garganacl 55. Bullet Punch priority +1 outspeeds all non-priority. Next turn: finish Venusaur with Bullet Punch + Politoed Ice Beam/Helping Hand, then handle opponent's back Pokémon with rain-protected Scizor.

decisions.rationale: Archaludon at 98% survives Garchomp's Stomping Tantrum (37-76%) and resists Raichu Thunderbolt (0.5x). Garganacl at 33% is guaranteed KO'd (min 35.3% > 33%). Save Garganacl's Purifying Salt for Venusaur's Sleep Powder later. Archaludon's Stamina also boosts Def on each hit taken.
decisions.notebook: Bullet Punch vs Garchomp is NEUTRAL (Steel does not SE Dragon). Close Combat vs Raichu: 56-117% max HP, not guaranteed KO at 58%; Sitrus Berry may save if damage <58%. Rain ended turn 7 (Politoed fainted); no rain protection for Scizor. Garchomp Stomping Tantrum guaranteed KOs Garganacl at 33% (min 35.3% > 33%); does 37-76% to Archaludon (survives at 98%). Raichu Encore locks Scizor into last used move (Bullet Punch); Raichu outspeeds Scizor so Encore lands first. Garganacl Purifying Salt = immune to Venusaur Sleep Powder; save for Venusaur matchup. Archaludon paralyzed Speed 61, SpA -2 from Draco Meteor; defensive pivot only, resists Thunderbolt 0.5x, weak to Dragon Claw and Stomping Tantrum 2x each. Scizor Close Combat vs Raichu neutral 1x. Key speed tiers: Raichu 143-178 > Garchomp 134-169 > Scizor 105 > Archaludon 61(par) > Garganacl 55. Bullet Punch priority +1 outspeeds all non-priority. Opponent back: Venusaur 50% (Sash broken, Chlorophyll, Sleep Powder/Leaf Storm/Sludge Bomb).

decisions.rationale: Venusaur cannot act through Bullet Punch, and consecutive Protect is unreliable. Preserve it for Politoed/Archaludon, bring Garchomp safely into the likely Bullet Punch, and force Garganacl to either fall to Thunderbolt or spend Protect while Garchomp enters.

decisions.notebook: Opponent team: Charizard-Mega-Y (Timid, CharizarditeY, HeatWave/Flamethrower/SolarBeam/Protect), Venusaur (Modest, FocusSash, Chlorophyll, SleepPowder/LeafStorm/SludgeBomb/Protect), Garchomp (Jolly, LifeOrb, RoughSkin, StompingTantrum/DragonClaw/RockSlide/Protect), Raichu (Timid, SitrusBerry, LightningRod, FakeOut/Nuzzle/Thunderbolt/Encore), Talonflame (Jolly, MentalHerb, GaleWings, not brought g1), Goodra-Hisui (Modest, Leftovers, SapSipper, not brought g1). Draco Meteor at SpA-2 + Expert Belt vs Garchomp ~48-105% max HP; combined with Bullet Punch chip + LO recoil KOs in nearly all lines. If Draco Meteor is blocked by Protect, SpA does NOT drop further (secondary effects require successful hit). Venusaur Focus Sash already broken (Ice Beam turn 4). Garganacl Purifying Salt = immune to Sleep Powder; save for Venusaur matchup. Key speed tiers: Raichu 143-178 > Garchomp 134-169 > Scizor 105 > Archaludon 61(par) > Garganacl 55. Bullet Punch priority+1 outspeeds all non-priority.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp is guaranteed faster than the paralyzed Archaludon and Stomping Tantrum is the clean super-effective removal. Thunderbolt gives the needed chip on Scizor for the remaining endgame; Rock Slide risks accuracy and leaves Archaludon alive to attack.
decisions.notebook: Opponent revealed: Politoed Drizzle/Sitrus with Hydro Pump, Ice Beam, Helping Hand, Protect; Archaludon Expert Belt/Stamina with Electro Shot, Flash Cannon, Draco Meteor, Protect, Modest; Garganacl Leftovers with Rock Slide, Wide Guard, Salt Cure, Protect; Mega Scizor Technician with Bullet Punch, U-turn, Close Combat, Protect. If Encore overrides Protect, Scizor still fires priority Bullet Punch and survives. Garganacl entering via Archaludon's slot avoids the likely Scizor-focused attacks. 3v2 advantage preserved for endgame.

decisions.rationale: Automatic: only one legal joint action.

Attack both low targets: Leaf Storm cleanly removes Archaludon if it does not Protect, while Thunderbolt removes Scizor if it does not Protect. Bullet Punch acts before Venusaur, but Venusaur’s intact Focus Sash prevents a one-hit denial. Their only full cover is double Protect; neither can safely repeat Protect next turn.

Bullet Punch priority guarantees Scizor acts first, chipping Venusaur to 7-31% (next-turn KO range). Draco Meteor at -2 SpA does 33-63% to Raichu (58% HP), possible KO. reflections.summary: Won through priority Bullet Punch chip from Mega Scizor and Archaludon's Draco Meteor sniping Garchomp and Raichu. The game was closer than it should have been—three of four Pokemon fainted and Archaludon survived at 20% paralyzed with -4 SpA. Sleep Powder missing twice on turns 11-12 was the margin; a single hit there could have ended the game. Garganacl contributed almost nothing, entering at 33% and dying immediately to Leaf Storm.
reflections.adjustment: Reconsider Garganacl as the fourth slot. It was brought to Wide Guard Heat Wave but never used it and died to a single Leaf Storm. Against a sun team with Venusaur+Garchomp, a fourth that pressures Venusaur or handles Garchomp better would be safer. Also lead differently if opponent swaps Raichu for Talonflame—Fake Out speed control won't be there but Tailwind will.
reflections.notebook: Opponent VGC series tendencies: brings sun core Zard-Y+Venusaur+Garchomp+Raichu; bench options Talonflame (Tailwind+Gale Wings priority) and Goodra-Hisui (SapSipper, Fire Blast). Venusaur = Focus Sash (broken g1, so sash fact only relevant if not brought or if healed). Raichu uses Encore (failed twice g1—may target Protect/locked moves next game). Garchomp is Life Orb Jolly (Stomping Tantrum over Earthquake suggests Archaludon/Scizor targeting). Opponent protects Venusaur aggressively and plays Sleep Powder even into bad matchups. For Game 2: expect possible Talonflame swap for speed control; if so, Bullet Punch priority matters more. Archaludon Expert Belt + Stamina; resists Leaf Storm, immune Sludge Bomb—hard Venusaur answer at full HP. Scizor-Mega Technician Bullet Punch is primary cleaner. Garganacl underperformed g1—evaluate whether it stays as 4th pick.

reflections.summary: Lost because the Charizard-Y/Venusaur sun plan was poorly suited to Politoed rain plus Scizor/Archaludon: Venusaur was heavily pressured by Bullet Punch and the final win condition became two failed Sleep Powders into Archaludon. The game was otherwise played cleanly.
reflections.adjustment: Reconsider bringing/committing to Mega Charizard Y into Politoed. For game 2, prioritize a four with reliable pressure on the rain-Steel core rather than a sun-dependent Venusaur endgame; if using the same four, preserve Garchomp and Raichu to remove Archaludon before Venusaur is exposed.
reflections.notebook: Opponent brought Politoed/Archaludon/Mega Scizor/Garganacl in G1, leaving Grimmsnarl and Noivern out. Their rain-Steel structure can overwrite Charizard Y’s weather, pressure Venusaur with Scizor Bullet Punch, and use Garganacl Wide Guard against spread pressure. Archaludon’s Stamina and bulky Expert Belt set remained a late-game threat even after Special Attack drops; prioritize eliminating it with Garchomp/Raichu support rather than relying on Sleep Powder.
